problem: The branch needed architecture hardening and Parking Jam optimization, while billiards still existed only as a contract. Pocket Club now needs a clean-room deterministic implementation, project-authored billiard-room presentation with visible shot controls, spatial rolling, audio feedback, typed routing, and a real multiplayer boundary without weakening the existing quality gates.
reuseDecision: Keep the existing hub, Personal Island, Modoki build, deterministic-domain conventions, and single feature branch. Add Pocket Club as focused domain/network/presentation owners; render rolling spheres through a presentation-only software sphere mapper; synthesize short collision sounds with Web Audio; reuse one event-based planar solver for both preview and execution; keep Colyseus behind a lazy session adapter and preserve Protobuf as the stable cross-language contract.
nonGoals: Copy Miniclip code, branding, textures, sounds, table artwork, or proprietary assets
Ship an authoritative Colyseus server in the same browser-client slice
Replace the existing Personal Island, Parking Jam, Junkyard Station, Modoki, or Three.js foundations
Turn the billiards presentation into a second physics or scoring implementation
acceptance: Every games/**/*.ts file has one architecture owner and all static and dynamic relative imports resolve through declared dependencies
Pocket Club collision, deterministic simulation, immutability, foul, group assignment, scratch, and eight-ball tests pass
The production hub exposes billiards through the Personal Island and ?game=billiards while preserving all existing routes
SolidJS mounts the billiards interface and Canvas 2D renders project-authored table, balls, guide, cue, and responsive controls
The browser contract executes a real break shot, observes movement, waits for rest, and captures every required viewport without runtime errors
The Colyseus adapter remains optional and lazy while billiards.proto preserves a versioned transport-neutral message contract
Pocket Club visibly renders seven potted-ball slots per player, a left vertical cue/power control, a right vertical direction control, and a circular spin control at every required viewport
Ball markings roll over a lit spherical surface according to table displacement rather than rotating as flat discs
A first user gesture unlocks project-authored Web Audio cues for cue strikes, ball contacts, cushion contacts, and pocket drops without external sound files
Source checks, strict typecheck, production build, bundle ratchet, and all browser contracts pass before publication
The unchanged base/startup bundle ratchet and explicit Pocket Club lazy-client and Colyseus chunk ratchets all pass
